title: Actually: Van Gogh Myths Busted
description: Popular stories about a tortured master—which hold up under scrutiny?

questions.question: Myth: Van Gogh only nicked his earlobe. Actually, how much of his left ear did he cut off?
questions.explanation: For decades scholars believed it was just the lobe. In 2016 a sketch by his doctor showed he removed nearly the whole ear with a razor.

questions.question: That 'almost all' evidence came from a 1930 sketch by which young doctor who treated him in 1888?
questions.explanation: Rey was a 23-year-old intern who saved Van Gogh's life. Van Gogh painted his portrait as thanks—Rey's mother reportedly used it to patch a chicken coop.

questions.question: Dr. Félix Rey treated Van Gogh at the hospital in which southern French town?
questions.explanation: Van Gogh moved to Arles in 1888 dreaming of an artists' colony. Gauguin's visit ended with the ear incident two days before Christmas.

questions.question: Myth: Van Gogh never sold a painting. Actually, in 1890 Anna Boch bought which canvas he painted near Arles?
questions.explanation: She bought it for about 400 francs at the Les XX exhibition in Brussels—the one sale every historian agrees on.

questions.question: Myth: The Red Vineyard was his only sale. Actually, Theo's 1888 letter records a Van Gogh self-portrait sold to dealers in what city?
questions.explanation: Theo wrote to the London dealers Sulley & Lori about a self-portrait they had bought. The work is lost, and some historians question the date—but it chips away at the 'only one sale' legend.
